<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">No other customers accounted for more than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000504" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis_us-gaapCustomerConcentrationRiskMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="2" scale="-2"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000505" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis_us-gaapCustomerConcentrationRiskMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="2" scale="-2"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000506" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis_us-gaapCustomerConcentrationRiskMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="2" scale="-2">10</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>% of product revenue or accounts receivable for the years ended December&#160;31, 2020, 2019, and 2018, respectively.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000364" name="us-gaap:ComprehensiveIncomePolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001419600_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.57%;text-indent:-3.57%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Comprehensive Loss</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Comprehensive loss includes net loss as well as other changes in stockholders&#8217; equity that result from transactions and economic events other than those with stockholders. The Company&#8217;s only element of other comprehensive income (loss) in all periods presented was unrealized gains (losses) on available-for-sale securities.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000365" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001419600_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.57%;text-indent:-3.57%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Income Taxes</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company accounts for income taxes using the asset and liability method. Under this method, deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the estimated future tax consequences of events that have been recognized in the financial statements or in the Company&#8217;s tax returns. Deferred taxes are determined based on the differences between financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax basis. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted rates in effect for the year in which these temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. Changes in deferred tax assets and liabilities are recorded in the provision for income taxes. The Company assesses the likelihood that its deferred tax assets will be recovered from future taxable income and, to the extent it believes, based upon the weight of available evidence, that it is more likely than not that all or a portion of deferred tax assets will not be realized, a valuation allowance is established through a charge to income tax expense. Potential recovery of deferred tax assets is evaluated by estimating the future taxable profits expected and considering prudent and feasible tax planning strategies.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company accounts for uncertainty in income taxes recognized in the financial statements by applying a two-step process to determine the amount of tax benefit to be recognized. First, the tax position must be evaluated to determine the likelihood that it will be sustained upon external examination by the taxing authorities. If the tax position is deemed more-likely-than-not to be sustained, the tax position is then assessed to determine the amount of benefit to recognize in the financial statements. The amount of benefit that may be recognized is the largest amount that has a greater than 50% likelihood of being realized upon ultimate settlement. The provision for income taxes includes the effects of any resulting tax reserves, or unrecognized tax benefits, that are considered appropriate as well as the related net interest and penalties.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000366" name="us-gaap:FairValueMeasurementPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001419600_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000366_dcnt_dc517f59-d24f-4df9-b93a-3bb83a0717fe">
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.57%;text-indent:-3.57%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fair Value Measurements</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fair value is defined as the exchange price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability (an exit price) in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset or liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. Valuation techniques used to measure fair value must maximize the use of observable inputs and minimize the use of unobservable inputs. Financial assets and liabilities carried at fair value are to be classified and disclosed in one of the following three levels of the fair value hierarchy, of which the first two are considered observable and the last is considered unobservable:</p>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:0.89%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:9.96%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;Level 1 &#8212;</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Quoted market prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities. Level 1 consists primarily of financial instruments whose value is based on quoted market prices, such as exchange-traded instruments and listed equities.</p></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:0.89%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:9.96%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;Level 2 &#8212;</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Observable inputs (other than Level 1 quoted prices) such as quoted prices in active markets for similar assets or liabilities, quoted prices in markets that are not active for identical or similar assets or liabilities, or other inputs that are observable or can be corroborated by observable market data.</p></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:0.89%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:9.96%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;Level 3 &#8212;</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Unobservable inputs that are supported by little or no market activity and that are significant to determining the fair value of the assets or liabilities, including pricing models, discounted cash flow methodologies and similar techniques.</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s financial instruments consist of cash equivalents, marketable securities, its term loan and 2024 Convertible Notes (Note 10). The estimated fair value of the Company&#8217;s financial instruments, with the exception of the 2024 Convertible Notes, approximates their carrying values.</p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">78</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000331_dcnt_a9f18ff7-c3f6-4d2b-bb70-de2e5cc40ee5" continuedAt="F_000331_dcnt_0ec3ed31-1731-4aa1-aa8d-3257939a046f"><ix:continuation id="F_000366_dcnt_dc517f59-d24f-4df9-b93a-3bb83a0717fe">
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair value of the 2024 Convertible Notes, which differs from their carrying value, is influenced by interest rates, stock price and stock price volatility and is determined by prices for the 2024 Convertible Notes observed in market trading. The market for trading of the 2024 Convertible Notes is not considered to be an active market and therefore the estimate of fair value is based on Level 2 inputs. The estimated fair value of the 2024 Convertible Notes, face value of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000507" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnTwoThousandTwentyFourConvertibleNotesMember_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">201.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000508" name="us-gaap:ConvertibleDebtFairValueDisclosures" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnTwoThousandTwentyFourConvertibleNotesMember_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">182.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million at December&#160;31, 2020.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000367" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001419600_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.57%;text-indent:-3.57%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Net Loss Per Share</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company follows the two-class method when computing net loss per share as the Company has issued shares that meet the definition of participating securities. The two-class method determines net loss per share for each class of common and participating securities according to dividends declared or accumulated and participation rights in undistributed earnings. The two-class method requires income available to common stockholders for the period to be allocated between common and participating securities based on their respective rights to receive dividends as if all income for the period had been distributed.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Basic net loss per share attributable to common stockholders is computed by dividing the net loss attributable to common stockholders by the weighted average number of shares of common stock outstanding for the period. Diluted net loss attributable to common stockholders is computed by adjusting net loss attributable to common stockholders to reallocate undistributed earnings based on the potential impact of dilutive securities, including the assumed conversion of our 2024 Convertible Notes, outstanding stock options and unvested restricted common stock, except where the result would be anti-dilutive. Diluted net loss per share attributable to common stockholders is computed by dividing the diluted net loss attributable to common stockholders by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding for the period, including potential dilutive common shares assuming the dilutive effect of the conversion of the 2024 Convertible Notes, the exercise of outstanding stock options and the vesting unvested restricted common stock. In the diluted net loss per share calculation, net loss would also be adjusted for the elimination of interest expense on the 2024 Convertible Notes, if the impact was not anti-dilutive. For periods in which the Company has reported net losses, diluted net loss per share attributable to common stockholders is the same as basic net loss per share attributable to common stockholders, since dilutive common shares are not assumed to have been issued if their effect is anti-dilutive. Potential common shares will always be anti-dilutive for periods in which the Company has reported a net loss. Diluted net loss per share attributable to common stockholders is the same as basic net loss per share attributable to common stockholders for the years ended December&#160;31, 2020, 2019, and 2018.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000368" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001419600_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.57%;text-indent:-3.57%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Segment Data</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company manages its operations as a single operating segment for the purposes of assessing performance and making operating decisions. The Company is a biopharmaceutical company focused on the development and commercialization of novel, local therapies. All revenues for the years ended December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019, were generated in the United States.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000369" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001419600_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000369_dcnt_46283b65-9ac8-42f7-a378-4f01448c346c">
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.57%;text-indent:-3.57%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.57%;text-indent:0%;;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Accounting Standards Recently Adopted</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In June&#160;2016, the FASB issued ASU&#160;No.&#160;2016-13,&#160;<span style="font-style:italic;">Financial Instruments - Credit Losses (Topic&#160;326): Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments</span> (&#8220;ASU&#160;2016-13&#8221;). The new standard requires entities to measure all expected credit losses for financial assets held at the reporting date based on historical experience, current conditions and reasonable and supportable forecasts. ASU&#160;2016-13 is effective for fiscal years, and the interim periods within those years, beginning after December&#160;15, 2019, and early adoption is permitted. The Company adopted this standard as of January&#160;1, 2020. The adoption of ASU&#160;2016-13 did not have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s condensed consolidated financial statements.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In July&#160;2018, the FASB issued ASU&#160;No.&#160;2018-13, <span style="font-style:italic;">Fair Value Measurement (Topic&#160;820): Disclosure Framework&#8212;Changes to the Disclosure Requirements for Fair Value Measurement</span> (&#8220;ASU&#160;2018-13&#8221;). The new standard modifies the disclosure requirements on fair value measurements in Topic&#160;820, Fair Value Measurement, as part of the FASB&#8217;s disclosure framework project. ASU&#160;2018-13 is effective for fiscal years, and the interim periods within those years, beginning after December&#160;15, 2019, and early adoption is permitted. Additionally, the new standard permits an entity to early adopt any removed or modified disclosures upon issuance of the ASU and delay adoption of the additional disclosures until their effective date. ASU&#160;2018-13 removes the requirement to disclose the amount of and reasons for transfers between Level 1 and Level 2 of the fair value hierarchy. The Company early adopted this portion of the standard as the quarter ended September&#160;30, 2018. The Company adopted the remainder of the standard as of January&#160;1, 2020. The adoption of the remainder of ASU&#160;2018-13 did not have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s condensed consolidated financial statements.</p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">79</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000331_dcnt_0ec3ed31-1731-4aa1-aa8d-3257939a046f"><ix:continuation id="F_000369_dcnt_46283b65-9ac8-42f7-a378-4f01448c346c">
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.57%;text-indent:0%;;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Accounting Standards Recently Issued</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In August&#160;2020, the FASB issued ASU&#160;No.&#160;2020-06, <span style="font-style:italic;">Debt &#8211; Debt with Conversion and Other Options</span> (&#8220;ASU&#160;2020-06&#8221;). The new standard simplifies the accounting for certain financial instruments with characteristics of liabilities and equity. The new guidance reduced the number of accounting models for convertible debt and convertible preferred stock instruments and made certain disclosure amendments intended to improve the information provided to users. The guidance also amended the derivative guidance for the &#8220;own stock&#8221; scope exception, which exempts qualifying instruments from being accounted for as derivatives if certain criteria are met. Finally, the standard changed the way certain convertible instruments are treated when calculating earnings per share. The standard is effective for the Company for fiscal years, and the interim periods within those years, beginning after December&#160;15, 2021, and early adoption is permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of ASU&#160;2020-06 on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements.</p></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000332" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001419600_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000332_dcnt_53817133-9c2b-4e1b-9acc-3e990a70d9f5">
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>

<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December&#160;31, 2020, the Company&#8217;s cash equivalents and marketable securities that are invested in money market funds are valued using Level 1 inputs based on quoted prices for identical securities in active markets. The Company measures the fair value of certain marketable securities using Level 2 inputs and primarily relies on quoted prices in active markets for similar marketable securities. Amortization and accretion of discounts and premiums are recorded in other income. As of December&#160;31, 2019, the Company&#8217;s cash equivalents, and marketable securities were classified within Level 2 of the fair value hierarchy due to the inputs utilized.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company had a term loan outstanding under its 2015 credit facility with MidCap Financial Funding XIII Trust and Silicon Valley Bank (the &#8220;2015 term loan&#8221;). On August&#160;2, 2019, the Company entered into an amended and restated credit and security agreement with Silicon Valley Bank as agent, MidCap Financial Trust, and Flexpoint MCLS Holdings, LLC (collectively, the &#8220;Lenders&#8221;), providing for a term loan of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000523" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandNineteenTermLoanMember_20190802" decimals="INF" scale="6">40.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million (the &#8220;2019 term loan&#8221;). The Company concurrently borrowed the $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000524" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandNineteenTermLoanMember_20190802" decimals="-5" scale="6">40.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million term loan and used $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000525" name="us-gaap:RepaymentsOfLinesOfCredit" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankAndMidCapFinancialFundingXIIITrustMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandFifteenTermLoanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">7.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of the proceeds to repay the remaining amount owed on the 2015 term loan. Pursuant to the amendment, the Company borrowed $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000527" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfSeniorLongTermDebt" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandNineteenTermLoanMember_20200517_20200518" decimals="-5" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000528" name="us-gaap:RepaymentsOfLinesOfCredit" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandNineteenTermLoanMember_20200517_20200518" decimals="-5" scale="6">15.0</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>&#160;million under a new term loan advance and immediately used the proceeds to repay an equal amount under the revolving credit facility, and the maximum principal amount of the revolving credit facility was reduced from $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000529" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumAmountOutstandingDuringPeriod" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandNineteenTermLoanMember_20200517_20200518" decimals="INF" scale="6">20.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000530" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumMonthendOutstandingAmount" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandNineteenTermLoanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="6">5.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. The new term loan is subject to substantially the same terms, including interest rate, amortization and maturity date, as the existing term loan under the credit facility. The amount outstanding on the 2019 term loan is reported at its carrying value in the accompanying balance sheet as of December&#160;31, 2020. The Company determined the fair value of the 2019 term loan using an income approach that utilizes a discounted cash flow analysis based on current market interest rates for debt issuances with similar remaining years to maturity, adjusted for credit risk. The 2019 term loan was valued using Level 2 inputs as of December&#160;31, 2020. The results of the calculation yielded a fair value that approximates its carrying value. The Company also concluded that the carrying value of the revolving credit facility approximated fair value because of the short-term maturity of this debt instrument.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On May&#160;2, 2017, the Company issued <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000533" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnTwoThousandTwentyFourConvertibleNotesMember_20170502" decimals="INF" scale="-2">3.375</ix:nonFraction>% convertible senior notes due 2024 (the &#8220;2024 Convertible Notes&#8221;) with embedded conversion features. The Company estimated the fair value of the 2024 Convertible Notes using a discounted cash flow approach to derive the value of a debt instrument using the expected cash flows and the estimated yield related to the convertible notes. The significant assumptions used in estimating the expected cash flows were: the estimated market yield based on an implied yield and credit quality analysis of a term loan with similar attributes, and the average implied volatility of the Company&#8217;s traded and quoted options available as of May&#160;2, 2017. <p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.57%;text-indent:0%;;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Amended and Restated Credit and Security Agreement</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:7.14%;text-indent:0%;;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Term Loan</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On August&#160;4, 2015, the Company entered into a credit and security agreement with MidCap Financial Trust, as agent, and MidCap Financial Funding XIII Trust and Silicon Valley Bank, as lenders, to borrow up to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000625" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnMidCapFinancialTrustMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandFifteenTermLoanMember_20150804" decimals="INF" scale="6">30.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in term loans. On August&#160;2, 2019, the Company terminated the credit and security agreement and concurrently entered into an amended and restated credit and security agreement (the &#8220;amended and restated credit and security agreement&#8221;) with Silicon Valley Bank as agent, MidCap Financial Trust, Flexpoint MCLS Holdings, LLC, and the other lenders from time to time party thereto (collectively, the &#8220;Lenders&#8221;), providing for a term loan of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000626" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandNineteenTermLoanMember_20190802" decimals="INF" scale="6">40.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and a revolving credit facility of up to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000628" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_20190802" decimals="INF" scale="6">20.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, both of which mature on <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000627" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentMaturityDate" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandNineteenTermLoanMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000629" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentMaturityDate" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">January&#160;1, 2024</ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric> (the &#8220;Maturity Date&#8221;). The Company concurrently borrowed the $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000630" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandFifteenTermLoanMember_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">40.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million term loan and used $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000631" name="us-gaap:RepaymentsOfLinesOfCredit" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandFifteenTermLoanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">7.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of the proceeds to repay the remaining amount owed on the 2015 term loan.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">82</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000338_dcnt_a1fd253e-fc78-4943-9445-afb13c67daf2" continuedAt="F_000338_dcnt_c4a37123-c7b1-4c7f-aca2-5d3e3178be90">

<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company granted the Lenders a security interest in substantially all of its personal property, rights and assets, other than intellectual property, to secure the payment of all amounts owed under the amended and restated credit and security agreement. The Company agreed not to encumber any of its intellectual property without the Lender&#8217;s prior written consent.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The amended and restated credit and security agreement contains certain representations, warranties, and covenants of the Company, including a minimum revenue covenant that will be in effect at any time the Company&#8217;s liquidity (defined as cash and cash equivalents and marketable securities held with Silicon Valley Bank and certain accounts receivables as deemed eligible under the amended and restated credit and security agreement) is below $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000632" name="flxn:DebtInstrumentCovenantMinimumCashAndCashEquivalents" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">80.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. Additionally, if the Company&#8217;s liquidity is below $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000633" name="flxn:DebtInstrumentCovenantMinimumCashAndCashEquivalents" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">80.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, all amounts received from customers collections will be applied immediately to reduce the revolving credit facility. As filed in the Form 8-K issued by the Company on May&#160;18, 2020, prior to May&#160;2021, the minimum revenue covenant, if it applies in the future, is set annually and is based on the greater of (i)&#160;a conservative percent of that year&#8217;s approved forecast and (ii)&#160;modest growth over the trailing twelve months of actual revenues. Beginning in May&#160;2021, the minimum revenue covenant, if it applies, will be the greatest of (i)&#160;a conservative percentage of that year&#8217;s approved forecast, (ii)&#160;modest growth over the trailing twelve months of actual revenues and (iii)&#160;<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000634" name="flxn:DebtInstrumentCovenantMinimumCashAndCashEquivalentsPercentage" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">100</ix:nonFraction>% of the minimum revenue covenant amount for the preceding month.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On May&#160;18, 2020, the Company borrowed $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000635" name="us-gaap:RepaymentsOfLinesOfCredit" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandNineteenTermLoanMember_20200517_20200518" decimals="-5" scale="6">15.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million under a new term loan advance and immediately used the proceeds to repay an equal amount under the revolving credit facility, and the maximum principal amount of the revolving credit facility was reduced from $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000636" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumAmountOutstandingDuringPeriod" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandNineteenTermLoanMember_20200517_20200518" decimals="INF" scale="6">20.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000637" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumMonthendOutstandingAmount" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandNineteenTermLoanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="6">5.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. The new term loan is subject to substantially the same terms, including interest rate, amortization and maturity dates, as the existing term loan under the credit facility.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The amended and restated credit and security agreement also has a material adverse event clause. If the revenue covenant becomes applicable and the Company fails to comply with it, or a material adverse change as defined in the agreement occurs, the amounts due under the amended and restated credit and security agreement could be declared immediately due and payable. As of December&#160;31, 2020, the Company was compliant with all covenants.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000638" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateTerms" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandNineteenTermLoanMember_20200101_20201231">Term loan borrowings under the credit facility accrue interest monthly at a floating interest rate equal to the greater of the prime rate plus 1.5% or 6.5% per annum.</ix:nonNumeric> Following an <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000639" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentPaymentTerms" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandNineteenTermLoanMember_20200101_20201231">interest-only period of <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000640" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentTerm" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentAxis_us-gaapInterestOnlyStripMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandNineteenTermLoanMember_20190802_20190802" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">18</ix:nonNumeric> months, principal is due in 36 equal monthly installments</ix:nonNumeric> commencing <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000642" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentDateOfFirstRequiredPayment1" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandNineteenTermLoanMember_20190802_20190802" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">February&#160;1, 2021</ix:nonNumeric>, and ending on the Maturity Date. Upon the Maturity Date, the Company will be obligated to pay a final payment equal to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000643" name="flxn:DebtInstrumentFinalPaymentPercentageOfAggregatePrincipalAmount" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnSiliconValleyBankMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandNineteenTermLoanMember_20201231" decimals="4" scale="-2">6.75</ix:nonFraction>% of the total principal amounts borrowed under the facility. The final payment amount is being accreted to the carrying value of the debt using the straight-line method, which approximates the effective interest method. As of December&#160;31, 2020, the carrying value of the term loan was approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000644" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebt" contextRef="C_0001419600_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">55.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, of which, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000645" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtCurrent" contextRef="C_0001419600_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">16.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million is due within 12 months and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000646" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnMidCapFinancialTrustMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_flxnTwoThousandFifteenTermLoanMember_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">39.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million is due in greater than 12 months.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company may prepay the term loan at any time by paying the outstanding principle balance, a final payment equal to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000647" name="flxn:DebtInstrumentFinalPaymentPercentageOfAggregatePrincipalAmount" contextRef="C_0001419600_20201231" decimals="4" scale="-2">6.75</ix:nonFraction>% of the term loan amount, all accrued interest and a prepayment fee of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000648" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentRedemptionPeriodAxis_us-gaapDebtInstrumentRedemptionPeriodOneMember_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">3</ix:nonFraction>% of the outstanding term loan amount if repaid in the first year, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000649" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentRedemptionPeriodAxis_us-gaapDebtInstrumentRedemptionPeriodTwoMember_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">2</ix:nonFraction>% of the outstanding term loan amount if repaid in the second year, and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000650" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentRedemptionPeriodAxis_us-gaapDebtInstrumentRedemptionPeriodThreeMember_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">1</ix:nonFraction>% of the outstanding term loan amount if repaid in the third year of the loan&#59; <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000651" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentRedemptionPeriodAxis_flxnDebtInstrumentRedemptionPeriodFourYearsAndThereafterMember_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="-2">no</ix:nonFraction> prepayment fee is required thereafter.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000379" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfMaturitiesOfLongTermDebtTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001419600_20200101_20201231" escape="true">

<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The 2024 Convertible Notes are considered convertible debt with a cash conversion feature. Per ASC&#160;470-20, <span style="font-style:italic;">Debt with Conversion and Other Options</span>, the Company has separated the convertible debt into liability and equity components based on the fair value of a similar debt instrument excluding the embedded conversion option. The carrying amount of the liability component was calculated by measuring the fair value of a similar liability that does not have an associated convertible feature. The allocation was performed in a manner that reflected our non-convertible debt borrowing rate for similar debt. The equity component of the 2024 Convertible Notes was recognized as a debt discount and represents the difference between the proceeds from the issuance of the 2024 Convertible Notes and the fair value of the liability of the 2024 Convertible Notes on their respective dates of issuance. The excess of the principal amount of the liability component over its carrying amount (&#8220;debt discount&#8221;) is amortized to interest expense using the effective interest method over <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000693" name="flxn:DebtInstrumentEffectiveInterestRatePeriod" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnTwoThousandTwentyFourConvertibleNotesMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">seven years</ix:nonNumeric>. <p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In connection with the issuance of the 2024 Convertible Notes, the Company incurred approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000694" name="us-gaap:PaymentsOfDebtIssuanceCosts" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnTwoThousandTwentyFourConvertibleNotesMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">6.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of debt issuance costs, which primarily consisted of underwriting, legal and other professional fees, and allocated these costs to the liability and equity components based on the allocation of the proceeds. Of the total debt issuance costs, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000695" name="flxn:DebtIssuanceCostsAllocatedToLiabilityComponent" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnTwoThousandTwentyFourConvertibleNotesMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">4.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million were allocated to the liability component and are recorded as a reduction of the 2024 Convertible Notes in our consolidated balance sheets. The remaining $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000696" name="flxn:DebtIssuanceCostsAllocatedToEquityComponentInReductionToAdditionalPaidInCapital" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnTwoThousandTwentyFourConvertibleNotesMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">2.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million was allocated to the equity component and is recorded as a reduction to additional paid-in capital.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Debt discount and issuance costs of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000697" name="us-gaap:UnamortizedDebtIssuanceExpense" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnTwoThousandTwentyFourConvertibleNotesMember_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">68.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million are being amortized to interest expense over the life of the 2024 Convertible Notes using the effective interest rate method. As of December&#160;31, 2020, the stated interest rate was <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000698" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnTwoThousandTwentyFourConvertibleNotesMember_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">3.375</ix:nonFraction>%, and the effective interest rate was <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000699" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateEffectivePercentage" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnTwoThousandTwentyFourConvertibleNotesMember_20201231" decimals="4" scale="-2">9.71</ix:nonFraction>%. Interest expense related to the 2024 Convertible Notes for the year ended December&#160;31, 2020, was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000700" name="us-gaap:InterestExpenseDebt" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnTwoThousandTwentyFourConvertibleNotesMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">15.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, including $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000701" name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfDebtDiscountPremium" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_flxnTwoThousandTwentyFourConvertibleNotesMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">8.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million related to amortization of the debt discount.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000380" name="us-gaap:ConvertibleDebtTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001419600_20200101_20201231" escape="true">

<p style="margin-bottom:5pt;margin-top:5pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair value of each stock option grant is estimated on the date of grant using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model. Expected volatility is based on historical volatility of the Company&#8217;s common stock. The expected term of the Company&#8217;s stock options has been determined utilizing the &#8220;simplified&#8221; method for awards that qualify as &#8220;plain vanilla&#8221; options. The expected term of stock options granted to non-employees is equal to the contractual term of the option award. The risk-free interest rate is determined by reference to the U.S. Treasury yield curve in effect at the time of grant of the award for time periods approximately equal to the expected term of the award. Expected dividend yield is based on the fact that the Company has never paid cash dividends and does not expect to pay any cash dividends in the foreseeable future. <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000381" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfShareBasedPaymentAwardStockOptionsValuationAssumptionsTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001419600_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000381_cnt_1">The relevant data used to determine the value of the stock option grants for the years ended December&#160;31, 2020, 2019, and 2018, is as follows:</ix:nonNumeric></p></ix:nonNumeric>

<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Included in the 2020 RSU awards was a grant of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_000815" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriod" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtTitleOfIndividualAxis_srtChiefExecutiveOfficerMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">175,000</ix:nonFraction> RSUs to the Company&#8217;s chief executive officer. These RSUs had a performance condition in that they would only vest if the Company reaches a certain revenue threshold for the year ending December&#160;31, 2020. If the threshold is reached, the RSUs vest in four substantially equal installments on each of the first four anniversaries of the vesting commencement date, subject to the employee&#8217;s continued employment with, or services to, the Company on each vesting date. This award was modified on July&#160;16, 2020, to take into account the impact of COVID-19 on the Company&#8217;s projected revenues. The modification changed the revenue thresholds and the portion of the RSUs that vest based on achieving the new thresholds. As a result of the modification, the Company concluded that it was probable that the performance condition would be met for at least a portion of the RSUs granted. Therefore, the Company recognized $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000816" name="flxn:StockBasedCompensationExpensePerformanceAwards" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of expense on these awards during the year ended December&#160;31, 2020. The remaining expense will be recognized over the remaining vesting term.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.57%;text-indent:0%;;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Operating Leases</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:7.14%;text-indent:0%;;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Burlington Lease</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In May&#160;2013, the Company entered into a lease for office space in Burlington, Massachusetts (the &#8220;Lease&#8221;) for an initial term of <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000840" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" contextRef="C_0001419600_20130531" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">42</ix:nonNumeric> months. In July&#160;2015, the Company amended the Lease to add additional square feet of office space and extend the term of the Lease through <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000841" name="us-gaap:LeaseExpirationDate1" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_stprMA_20150701_20150731" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">October&#160;31, 2019</ix:nonNumeric>. On April&#160;7, 2017, the Company further amended the Lease to add additional square feet of office space and extend the term to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000842" name="flxn:LeaseExpirationDateForTemporarySpace" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_stprMA_20170406_20170407" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">October&#160;31, 2023</ix:nonNumeric>.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Upon adoption of ASU&#160;2016-02, the Company recorded a right-of-use asset and corresponding lease liability for the Lease on January&#160;1, 2019, by calculating the present value of lease payments, discounted at <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000843" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseDiscountRate" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_countryMA_20181231" decimals="3" scale="-2">8.9</ix:nonFraction>%, the Company&#8217;s estimated incremental borrowing rate, over the remaining term of the Lease.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In June&#160;2019, the Company amended the Lease to add additional square feet of office space and extend the term of the Lease through <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000845" name="us-gaap:LeaseExpirationDate1" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_countryMA_20190601_20190630" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">April&#160;30, 2025</ix:nonNumeric> (the &#8220;Amended Lease&#8221;). As a result of the Amended Lease, the total rentable floor area is <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_utrsqft" id="F_000844" name="flxn:OperatingLeaseOfficeSpace" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_countryMA_20190630" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">41,873</ix:nonFraction> square feet. Starting in August&#160;2019, the Company&#8217;s minimum monthly lease payment is approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000846" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeasesRentExpenseMinimumRentals" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_countryMA_20190601_20190630" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">108,000</ix:nonFraction>. which increases over the term of the Amended Lease. In addition to the base rent for the office space, the Company is responsible for its share of operating expenses and real estate taxes. The lease commencement date for the additional space, which represents the date the Company first had access to the space, was <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000847" name="flxn:LeaseCommencementDateForAdditionalSpace" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_countryMA_20190601_20190630" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">July&#160;1, 2019</ix:nonNumeric>. The Company accounted for the Amended Lease as a lease modification that is a separate contract from the original lease and recorded an incremental right-of-use asset and lease liability of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000849" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseLiability" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_countryMA_20190630" decimals="INF" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000848" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_countryMA_20190630" decimals="INF" scale="6">2.5</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, which represents the present value of the lease payments relating to the new space, as well as the lease payments relating to the 18-month extension of the existing space, as of the modification date, discounted at <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000850" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseDiscountRate" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_countryMA_20190630" decimals="INF" scale="-2">6.8</ix:nonFraction>%.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The straight-line lease cost for the Amended Lease (including the expense relating to the original Lease) amounted to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000851" name="flxn:StraightLineOperatingLeaseCost" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_countryMA_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">1.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2020, respectively, and was included in operating expenses. As of December&#160;31, 2020, the remaining lease term on the Amended Lease was <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000852" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseWeightedAverageRemainingLeaseTerm1" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_countryMA_20201231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">4.3</ix:nonNumeric> years, which includes the <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000853" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRenewalTerm" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_countryMA_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">18</ix:nonNumeric>-month extension resulting from the amendment signed in June&#160;2019.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:7.14%;text-indent:0%;;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Woburn Lease</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In February&#160;2017, the Company entered into a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000854">five-year</span> lease for laboratory space located in Woburn, Massachusetts with a monthly lease payment of approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000855" name="flxn:OperatingLeaseMonthlyPayment" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_flxnWoburnMassachusettsMember_20170201_20170228" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">15,000</ix:nonFraction>, which increases over the term of the lease, plus a share of operating expenses.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Upon adoption of ASU&#160;2016-02, the Company recorded a right-of-use asset and corresponding lease liability for the Lease on January&#160;1, 2019, by calculating the present value of lease payments, discounted at <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000856" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseDiscountRate" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_flxnWoburnMassachusettsMember_20181231" decimals="3" scale="-2">8.4</ix:nonFraction>%, the Company&#8217;s estimated </p></ix:nonNumeric>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000342_dcnt_9d77f1d3-9584-4f29-b109-7a2724b8c0a3" continuedAt="F_000342_dcnt_ca71d5fe-523d-424b-9233-c4eb82fd666f">
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">incremental borrowing rate, over the remaining term. </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000857" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseOptionToExtend" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_flxnWoburnMassachusettsMember_20200101_20201231">The Woburn lease includes an option to extend the term of the lease for two years</ix:nonNumeric></span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">. Since the Company adopted </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ASU&#160;</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2016-02 using the Comparatives under 840 approach, it did not reassess the determination of its operating leases as leases, and therefore no options to extend the lease were included in the calculation of the lease liability as of</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">December&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">. The straight-line lease cost for the Woburn lease amounted to </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">$</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000858" name="flxn:StraightLineOperatingLeaseCost" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_flxnWoburnMassachusettsMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.2</ix:nonFraction></span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;million</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> for the </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">year ended December&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">, respectively, and was included in operating expenses. As of </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">December&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">, the remaining lease term on the Woburn lease was </span><span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000859" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseWeightedAverageRemainingLeaseTerm1" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_flxnWoburnMassachusettsMember_20201231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">1.2</ix:nonNumeric> </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">years</span></span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">.</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company incurred operating lease costs of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000860" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseCost" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_flxnWoburnMassachusettsMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">2.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000861" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseCost" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_flxnWoburnMassachusettsMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">2.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000862" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseCost" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_flxnWoburnMassachusettsMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">1.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million for the years ended December&#160;31, 2020, 2019, and 2018, respectively.</p>
<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.57%;text-indent:0%;;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Manufacturing and Supply Agreement with Patheon U.K. Limited</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In July&#160;2015, the Company and Patheon U.K. Limited (&#8220;Patheon&#8221;) entered into a Manufacturing and Supply Agreement (the &#8220;Manufacturing Agreement&#8221;) and Technical Transfer and Service Agreement (the &#8220;Technical Transfer Agreement&#8221;) for the manufacture of ZILRETTA.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Patheon agreed in the Technical Transfer Agreement to undertake certain transfer activities and construction services needed to prepare Patheon&#8217;s United Kingdom facility for the commercial manufacture of ZILRETTA in dedicated manufacturing suites. The Company provided Patheon with certain equipment and materials necessary to manufacture ZILRETTA and pays Patheon a monthly fee for such activities and reimburses Patheon for certain material, equipment and miscellaneous expenses and additional services.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The initial term of the Manufacturing Agreement is <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000863" name="flxn:ManufacturingServicesAndSupplyAgreementPeriod" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapLossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis_flxnManufacturingAndSupplyAgreementWithPatheonUKLimitedMember_20150701_20150731" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> years from approval by the FDA of the Patheon manufacturing suites for ZILRETTA, or until October&#160;6, 2027. The Company pays a monthly base fee to Patheon for the operation of the manufacturing suites and a per product fee for each vial based upon a forecast of commercial demand. The Company also reimburses Patheon for purchases of materials and equipment made on its behalf, certain nominal expenses and additional services. The Manufacturing Agreement will remain in full effect unless and until it expires or is terminated. Upon termination of the Manufacturing Agreement (other than termination by Flexion in the event that Patheon does not meet the construction and manufacturing milestones or for a breach by Patheon), Flexion will be obligated to pay for the costs incurred by Patheon associated with the removal of our manufacturing equipment and for Patheon&#8217;s termination costs up to a capped amount.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Manufacturing Agreement with Patheon contains an operating lease for the use of dedicated manufacturing suites. With the adoption of ASU&#160;2016-02, the Company recorded a right-of-use asset and corresponding lease liability for the operating lease.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In June&#160;2019, the Company and Patheon amended the Manufacturing Agreement and the Technical Transfer Agreement. The amendment primarily modifies the compensation structure, which is comprised of base fees and per product fees the Company pays to Patheon and does not result in any additional rights of use. The Company accounted for the amendment as a lease modification that is not a separate contract from the original lease. As part of the modification, the Company reassessed whether the contract is or contains a lease and determined that there is an operating lease component for the use of dedicated manufacturing suites. The remainder of the consideration is allocated to the service component. The Company also reassessed the lease liability by calculating the present value of the remaining lease payments as of the modification date, discounted at <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000864" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseDiscountRate" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapLossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis_flxnManufacturingAndSupplyAgreementWithPatheonUKLimitedMember_20190630" decimals="3" scale="-2">6.1</ix:nonFraction>%. The modification resulted in an increase to each of the lease liability and right of use asset of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000866" name="flxn:IncreaseDecreaseInOperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapLossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis_flxnManufacturingAndSupplyAgreementWithPatheonUKLimitedMember_20190601_20190630" decimals="-5" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000865" name="flxn:IncreaseDecreaseInOperatingLeaseLiability" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapLossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis_flxnManufacturingAndSupplyAgreementWithPatheonUKLimitedMember_20190601_20190630" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.5</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>&#160;million.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In April&#160;2020, the Company entered into a side letter amending the Manufacturing Agreement with Patheon pursuant to which the parties agreed that the Company would continue to pay the monthly base fee for maintaining the manufacturing suites, but minimum purchase obligations would be cancelled for 2020 as the Company temporarily suspended manufacturing activities for ZILRETTA. In June&#160;2020, the Company informed Patheon of its intent to restart manufacturing in the fourth quarter. The amendment did not change the amount of fixed consideration owed to Patheon over the life of the contract, nor did it grant the Company any additional rights of use. As such, there was no change in the accounting for the embedded lease as a result of this amendment.</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December&#160;31, 2020, the remaining lease term on the Patheon lease was <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000868" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseWeightedAverageRemainingLeaseTerm1" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapLossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis_flxnManufacturingAndSupplyAgreementWithPatheonUKLimitedMember_20201231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">6.8</ix:nonNumeric> years. The straight-line lease cost amounted to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000867" name="flxn:StraightLineOperatingLeaseCost" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapLossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis_flxnManufacturingAndSupplyAgreementWithPatheonUKLimitedMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2020, respectively, and is included in inventory as part of manufacturing overhead.</p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">89</p>

<p style="margin-top:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.57%;text-indent:0%;;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Other Commitments and Contingencies</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:7.14%;text-indent:0%;;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Evonik Supply Agreement</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In November&#160;2016, the Company entered into a Supply Agreement with Evonik Corporation (&#8220;Evonik&#8221;) for the purchase of PLGA which is used in the manufacturing of potential clinical and commercial supply of ZILRETTA. Pursuant to the Supply Agreement, Flexion is obligated to submit rolling monthly forecasts to Evonik for PLGA supply, a portion of which will constitute binding orders. In addition, Flexion agreed to certain minimum purchase requirements and which do not apply (i)&#160;during periods in which Evonik is in material breach of the Supply Agreement or is unable to perform its obligations due to a force majeure event, (ii)&#160;with respect to orders that Evonik is unable to supply in excess of binding orders, (iii)&#160;for orders Evonik is unable to timely deliver or does not deliver conforming product and provides a credit for such order, or (iv)&#160;during an uncured material quality failure by Evonik. Flexion agreed to purchase PLGA batches at a specified price per gram in U.S. dollars, subject to adjustment from time to time, including due to changes in price indices and in the event the initial term of the Supply Agreement is extended. The total term of the agreement is <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000885" name="flxn:SupplyAgreementPeriod" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapRelatedPartyTransactionAxis_flxnEvonikCorporationMember_20161101_20161130" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">five years</ix:nonNumeric>. Upon termination of the Supply Agreement (other than termination due to the expiration of the term of the agreement or due to bankruptcy of either Evonik or Flexion), Flexion is obligated to pay the costs associated with the binding supply forecast provided to Evonik. <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000888" name="us-gaap:SignificantSupplyCommitmentDescription" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapRelatedPartyTransactionAxis_flxnEvonikCorporationMember_20200101_20201231">The Supply Agreement will renew for <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_flxnTerm" id="F_000887" name="flxn:NumberOfRenewalTerms" contextRef="C_0001419600_us-gaapRelatedPartyTransactionAxis_flxnEvonikCorporationMember_20161101_20161130" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">two</ix:nonFraction> successive <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000886">two-year</span> terms upon mutual written consent by both parties.</ix:nonNumeric></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:7.14%;text-indent:0%;;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Southwest Research Institute License Agreement</p>
<p style="margin-top:5pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On July&#160;25, 2014, the Company entered into an exclusive worldwide license agreement with Southwest Research Institute (&#8220;SwRI&#8221;) with respect to the use of SwRI&#8217;s proprietary microsphere manufacturing technologies for certain steroids formulated with PLGA, including ZILRETTA. Under the agreement, the Company paid an upfront fee of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000889" name="flxn:ContractualObligationUpfrontFeePaid" contextRef="C_0001419600_srtCounterpartyNameAxis_flxnSouthWestResearchInstituteMember_srtProductOrServiceAxis_flxnZilrettaMember_us-gaapResearchAndDevelopmentArrangementContractToPerformForOthersByTypeAxis_us-gaapLicenseAgreementTermsMember_20140724_20140725" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">120,000</ix:nonFraction> to SwRI. In February&#160;2017, Flexion executed an agreement with SwRI to transfer manufacturing equipment to SwRI in consideration for SwRI deeming the additional milestone payment to have been fully paid by Flexion.</p>

The Baylor license agreement grants </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">the Company </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">an exclusive, royalty-bearing, world-wide right and license (with a right to sublicense) for human applications under its patent and other proprietary rights directly related to FX201, with a similar non-exclusive license to certain Baylor intellectual property rights that are not specific to FX201. The license agreement with Baylor includes a low single-digit royalty on net sales of FX201 and requires </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">the Company </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">to use reasonable efforts to develop FX201 according to timelines set out in the license agreement.
